reason: A is the better, more novel and mechanistically plausible extension: it tests whether a reported low-energy glass-to-glass transition can stabilize a phosphorus-containing amorphous HEA, whereas B largely repeats the cited melt-spinning result and does not justify why faster quenching would increase the thermal stability of the resulting high-fictive-temperature glass. A’s main weakness is that post-quench annealing can improve crystallization resistance but not glass-forming ability during the original solidification, so that claim and the decisive experiment would need refinement.
